heroHeadline: JNIM Issues Coalition Manifesto Targeting FAMa Defections as Bamako Blockade Tightens — Day 7 of Siege
heroSubtitle: On April 30–May 1, 2026, JNIM issued a broad political manifesto calling on all Malian society — FAMa soldiers, political parties, religious leaders — to join a common front against the junta, in an unprecedented shift from purely jihadist to national-liberation messaging. The US Embassy confirmed hundreds of vehicles stranded at Bamako entry points in a 'Reported Blockades' security alert issued April 30. Regional analysts in Ghana and across West Africa warned that JNIM's operational sophistication — combining military offensive, negotiated exit deals, and political propaganda simultaneously — has materially accelerated the timeline for jihadist spillover into coastal states. Bamako remains under nightly curfew; fuel at 940 CFA/L; JNIM holds Tessit, FLA holds Kidal, and ISGS besieges FAMa in Ménaka's former UN camp. Russia rejected withdrawal on April 30 and pledged to continue operations. The Goïta junta has not publicly responded to the coalition manifesto.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, RFI, Le Monde, Crisis Group, UN OHCHR, HRW, SIPRI, AFP, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Long War Journal, Africa Center for Strategic Studies, Institute for Economics & Peace, and US Embassy Bamako. All figures approximate unless stated.
